matches.rationale: GT1 concerns inflated/unrealistic benchmark results in Figure 9 and Section 4.2 with insufficient variance reporting. The findings discuss various inconsistencies but none specifically address the unrealistic favorability or lack of confidence intervals in the benchmark results of Figure 9.

GT2 identifies inconsistency between claimed 2× latency reduction and the actual computational overhead (roughly doubling prefill computation). Pred_id 9 directly addresses this, noting Section 3.4 claims 'roughly twice the computational cost' but Figure 8(b) shows varying overhead from 1× to 1.27×, not consistently 2×.

GT3 criticizes applying non-uniform head-budget allocation to baselines (claimed as fair) while baselines were designed for uniform budgets, creating asymmetric conditions. Pred_id 10 directly identifies this issue in Section 4.1, noting the unfair comparison where KVzip uses superior allocation while baselines use inferior uniform settings.

GT4 concerns exaggerated claims in the abstract about 'negligible performance loss' and 'significantly outperforms' that aren't fully substantiated. Pred_id 6 identifies this inconsistency between Section 1's claim of 'negligible performance loss' and Section 4.2/figures showing significant degradation at aggressive compression ratios.
GT5 concerns a fabricated reference to Corallo et al. [14] in the Related Work section. None of the findings mention this specific citation issue or fabricated reference problem.

GT6 concerns the omission of ethical implications and mitigation strategies for privacy leakage risks identified in Section 4.3/Table 1. While findings mention Table 1 data, none specifically address the missing ethical discussion or mitigation strategies in the main body.

GT7 concerns overly positive rhetoric in the Conclusion with unqualified definitive claims. None of the findings specifically address rhetorical manipulation or unsupported definitive language in the Conclusion section.

GT8 identifies mismatch between Introduction claims of maintaining accuracy at 70% eviction and mixed empirical results in Section 4.2. Pred_id 6 captures this same issue, noting the inconsistency between claims of 'negligible performance loss' and actual substantial accuracy drops shown in figures.

GT9 concerns optimistic/under-reported compression overhead in Figure 8b (peak memory ~30-38GB claimed but likely higher). Pred_id 8 directly addresses this, noting Figure 8(b) shows 48.3-62.3 GB peak memory with 10-14 GB overhead that is not 'negligible' as claimed.

GT10 concerns overly positive rhetorical language in the Introduction ('novel', 'particularly benefits', etc.) without acknowledging limitations. While findings note various claim issues, none specifically address the rhetorical manipulation in the Introduction's presentation language.

GT11 concerns missing IRB/consent disclosures and conflict-of-interest statements for sensitive datasets in the main body. None of the findings address missing ethical disclosures, IRB statements, or funding transparency issues.

GT12 concerns removal/alteration of Table 1 entry showing privacy leakage (phone number revelation), sanitizing contradictory evidence. The findings mention Table 1 in other contexts but don't identify missing or altered privacy-revealing examples.

GT13 identifies inconsistencies in Section 3.2 attention matrix descriptions and dimension errors in Equation (2). Pred_id 1 directly identifies the dimension error in Equation (2) (maximization over wrong range), and Pred_id 5 notes unclear slicing operations and dimension inconsistencies in the same section.

GT14 concerns systematic exaggeration in Section 4 figures showing KVzip outperforming baselines by unrealistic margins. While findings note various data inconsistencies, none specifically address the systematic exaggeration of comparative performance across multiple figures in Section 4.

GT15 concerns omission/weakening of Appendix Section B discussing ethical implications, privacy risks, and limitations. None of the findings address missing or weakened content in the Appendix's ethical discussion section.
